content.comment_body: Hello, a friend asked me to help identify an issue with a project he created using [product_name] version [version_no]. He sent images and the project file. I didn't notice anything unusual in the program except that he added some high contacts to prevent unconnected contacts, as he described, but it still didn't function properly. The issue is this: the program seems fine during simulation on the PC. Transfer to the PLC works with no errors. However, when he uploads the program back from the PLC to his computer, he sees many unconnected contacts, always missing the connection from the first contact on the left. He tried forcing connections with high contacts, which briefly worked, but others became disconnected instead, so that wasn't a viable solution. Also, the unconnected contacts don't show up using the 'go to' search function. Simulating the problematic program shows that even with a high contact before them, if these contacts are active, voltage doesn't pass through. I hope I've explained his issue clearly. I'll share the project and some images. Thank you in advance for your assistance.

Hi, the only solution I know is to open the project in LDD mode and then switch to FBD mode. The issue might be caused by copying and pasting only parts of function blocks in LDD mode. If you program directly in FBD, this issue shouldn't occur.

Thank you for your response. I told my friend to try that, but he doesn't understand FBD and was hoping for a solution that didn't involve changing modes. I suggested redoing the connections missing in the PLC, but he said that didn't help. He believes this might be a software bug or a mistake in his program. He also tried converting from LDD to FBD and downloading to the PLC, but the issue persisted. Thanks again for your help.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are facing a problem where connections in a project created with [product_name] version [version_no] appear as unconnected after uploading from the PLC to the PC, even though simulations and transfers to the PLC work without errors. Efforts to fix the issue manually or by switching programming modes have not resolved it, suggesting possible inconsistencies in the editor or a software bug.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the program's connections to be reliably displayed and preserved after transferring between PC and PLC using [product_name], without any loss or corruption of programmed logic.
